draft.title: The cosine rule
card: In any triangle, c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C. Angle C is the angle between sides a and b, and c is the side opposite it.
Use it to find the third side when you know two sides and the angle between them. Example: a = 5, b = 7, C = 60° gives c² = 25 + 49 − 70 × 0.5 = 39, so c = 6.2.
Use it to find an angle when you know all three sides. Rearrange it: cos C = (a² + b² − c²) ÷ 2ab. Side c is the one opposite the angle you want.
Work out 2ab cos C as one amount, subtract it from a² + b², and take the square root last.
draft.remember: Two sides and the angle between, or three sides: use the cosine rule.

a.q: Two trails leave a campsite at an angle of 60°. One is 6 km long and the other is 10 km long. How far apart are their ends, to 1 decimal place?
a.why: c² = 6² + 10² − 2 × 6 × 10 × cos 60° = 136 − 60 = 76, so c = 8.7 km. Stopping at 76 forgets the square root.
a.clue: The 60° angle sits between the two known sides.

b.q: A garden bed is a triangle with sides 5 m, 6 m and 7 m. What is the angle opposite the 7 m side, to 1 decimal place?
b.why: cos C = (5² + 6² − 7²) ÷ (2 × 5 × 6) = 12 ÷ 60 = 0.2, so C = 78.5°. The 7 m side must be c, the side opposite the angle. Using 101.5° comes from a sign error that makes cos C negative.
b.clue: The side opposite the wanted angle is the one that is subtracted.

check.summary: No problems found. The card example (c ≈ 6.2), question a (√76 ≈ 8.7 km) and question b (cos C = 0.2, so C ≈ 78.5°) all check out, and the explanations match the card.
